summary: Cron-synchronized surge causing second-scale 429 waves on dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary:
Nimbus Analytics is observing concentrated 429 responses in tight 8-25s windows when their orchestrator launches many short-lived inference requests at the same instant. Responses include Retry-After headers and are returned from tenant-level soft throttles.

Impact:
- Ingestion/backfill jobs see 3-6% error spikes during the burst windows, triggering requeue churn and delayed downstream processing.
- Latency-sensitive inference calls intermittently fail for a few seconds, while long-running batch tasks are largely unaffected outside burst windows.

This pattern appears tied to the tenant token-bucket refill granularity plus connection reuse that concentrates logical requests into the same refill epoch.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure Nimbus orchestrator in prod-us-west to run synchronized batch starts (cron without jitter).
2) Start 600 short requests (avg 200-350ms) across 100 worker processes within one second. Keep HTTP/2 keepalives and high stream multiplexing on.
3) Observe ephemeral 429 waves lasting 8-25 seconds with Retry-After: 1 or 2.
4) Repeat with jittered starts (>=300ms) and reduced per-connection streams to confirm mitigation.

This reliably reproduces when orchestration starts are tightly synchronized and connection reuse is aggressive.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypotheses:
- Short refill epoch (1s) combined with synchronized starts exhausts tenant bucket for several contiguous seconds.
- HTTP/2 connection multiplexing aggregates many logical requests into a small set of connections; token accounting at request boundaries plus coarse refills produces sawtooth behavior.
- Probable amplification from client retries that land in the same epochs.

Collected evidence:
- Metric spikes in token debit match the scheduled cron start times.
- Ingress proxy traces show disproportionate stream counts on a handful of client connections from Nimbus.
- Testbed reproduction with per-connection accounting enabled shows epoch-aligned exhaustion when requests are tightly clustered.

Conclusion so far: Coordinated orchestration starts and connection reuse are the leading contributors; client-side retries worsen the waves. Infra-level options considered include finer refill granularity and per-stream accounting changes.
short_term_workaround:
- Recommend Nimbus enable randomized jitter (200-800ms) for scheduled starts to desynchronize worker launches.
- Advise reducing max concurrent streams per HTTP/2 connection (suggest 4-6) for hosts that make many short calls.
- Implement client retry policy with exponential backoff + jitter to avoid retry storms.
- SRE temporarily increased tenant burst allowance (+30%) for 48 hours to reduce immediate impact while customer applies client changes.
resolution:
Temporary actions applied 2026-03-13:
- Tenant burst pool increased by SRE for 48 hours (+30%).
- Support delivered an implementation checklist to Nimbus: add jitter, cap per-connection streams, and apply jittered exponential backoff in SDK.

Permanent follow-ups:
- ENG: Evaluate rate-limiter epoch sizing and options for smoother microburst handling (ENG-6891).
- Product: Add console guidance that warns Dedicated customers about synchronized start patterns and provides recommended manifest.
- CS: Draft an orchestrator best-practices bullet list for customers with heavy short-request workloads.

Status: Waiting on Nimbus confirmation. Customer reported preliminary improvement after applying jitter and stream caps; ask to validate for 72 hours before resolving.
